rows.author: C018
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING PREFERENTIAL PROTECTION TO INVENTORS APPLYING FOR PATENTS ON INVENTIONS WHICH AFFECT NATIONAL INTEREST, ESTABLISHING A FUND THEREFOR, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION OF THE CONFIDENTIALITY OF SUCH APPLICATIONS DURING THE PERIOD OF APPLICATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CODE
rows.abstract: The Philippines is blessed with creative minds. Although largely unrecognized , it is nevertheless true that many Filipinos have created inventions which could have brought not only honors to our country but socio-economic benefits as well. Unfortunately, two serious problems face our inventors, the first is lack of support, financial or otherwise, from the government, and second  is intense and often-malicious objection and opposition from sectors which stand to lose were such inventions everto see the light of day.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 1999-11-10

rows.author: C088
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL CENTER FOR EXCELLENCE IN SPORTS (NCES) UNDER THE PHILIPPINE SPORTS COMMISSION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The dismal failure of our national athletes to improve their medal standing in the recently concluded South East Asian Games signals the need to refocus the thrust in our sports programs and policies.  The proposed creation of the NCES aims to centralize all training programs undertaken by various government agencies and sports organizations under one umbrella.  It shall seek to provide wolrd calss training facilities for our atheltes. Furthermore, the athletes shall be provided withthe proper training and enticing incentives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 1999-11-15

rows.author: C088
rows.title_full: AN ACT SEPARATING AND CONVERTING THE COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING AND ARCHITECTURE LOCATED AT THE MUNICIPALITY OF JOSE PANGANIBAN, PROVINCE OF CAMARINES NORTE, INTO CAMARINES NORTE INSTITUTE OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY INDEPENDENT FROM THE CAMARINES NORTE STATE COLLEGE AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7352 AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

rows.author: C088
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING MARKET INFORMATION CENTERS THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The establishment of provincial/city /municipal market information centers providing realistic marketing information systems and which may serve as trade centers as well, would vastly contribute on encouraging favorable marketing chances for farm produce such as pineapples, vegetables, rootcrops, and other high value crops including livestocks and poultry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1999-11-15

rows.author: C094
rows.title_full: AN ACT MAKING THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND THEIR OFFICIALS OR EMPLOYEES LIABLE FOR DEATH OF, OR INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO PROPERTY CAUSED BY THEIR RESPECTIVE OFFICIALS OR EMPLOYEES DUE TO THE NEGLIGENT ACT OR OMISSION TO PERFORM THEIR DUTIES AS MANDATED BY LAW OR ORDINANCES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 2180 OF THE NEW CIVIL CODE
rows.abstract: Rationale: The great loss of precious human lives at a recent Cherry Hills subdivision mishap and the past tragic fire that struck Ozone Disco in Quezon City speak of palpable and gross negligence and tortuous performance of official duties of somegovernment officials tasked to regulate housing subdivisions and buildings of business establishments in the country. Precious lives could have been saved from disasters had our government officials and employees been performing their duties conscientiously with due regards to the safety and welfare of the public.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1999-11-15

rows.author: C094
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE COMPULSORY MOTOR VEHICLES LIABILITY INSURANCE FEE FROM FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (P5,000.00) TO THIRTY THOUSAND PESOS (P30,000.00) FOR DEATH CLAIM AND NOT EXCEEDING TEN THOUSAND PESOS (P10,000.00) FOR PHYSICAL INJURY CLAIM, TO INDEMNIFY THE DEATH OR BODILY INJURY OF A PASSENGER OR THIRD PARTY, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 378, CHAPTER VI OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1460, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INSURANCE CODE OF 1978
rows.abstract: Ratinale: In 1998, the peso's purchasing power has gone down to P0.34. Conversely, the real value of P5,000 ia only P1,700. The decline was further aggravated following the recent spate of price increases in oil, transport fare, electricity, tuitionfee, prime commodities, and the skyrocketeing increase in toll rates. > It is in this context that this bill is filed to increase the said amount from P5,000.00 to P30,000.00 for death claim and not exceeding P10,000.00 for physical injury claim.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1999-11-15

rows.author: C094
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REQUIRE THE LABELING OF IMPORTED MEAT AND MEAT FOOD PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: "Meat Labeling Act of 1999" This bill substantiates the policy of the State t protect the interests of the consumer against deceptive, unfair, and unconscionable sales acts and practices, to adopt measures to ensure pure and safe supply of importedmeat and meat food products in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 1999-11-15

rows.author: C094
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT OF ELDERLY MEMBERS OF THE FAMILY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Maintenance of Parents Act of 1999" Children shall maintain and support their father or mother and other direct ascendants who are in need. Where an elderly member appears to be in need, he may by himself or through a representative of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), file a petition in court for his maintenance and support from any or all of his children. Upon trial, elderly member shall be represented by a lawyer from the public attorney's office and shall be exempt from all charges and fees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 1999-11-15

rows.author: C094
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF COMPENSATION TO BUILDERS AND CONTRACTORS OF BUILD-OPERATE-T RANSFER (BOT) PROJECTS, WHICH ENHANCE THE VALUE OF LANDS OR PROPERTY
rows.abstract: The State shall formulate and implement policies and programs to provide a system of compensation to BOT investors whose projects resulted the increase in the value of land.  These investors shall be compensated by the property owner, or in case ofpublic lands, by the local government unit or the national government, through an equitable reimbursement based on a percentage of the realized gain or increase in value attributable to said development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 1999-11-15

rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTRUCTURING THE OIL INDUSTRY BY ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL OIL EXCHANGE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Within three (3) months from the efectivity of this Act, a government-owne d and controlled corporation to be named as the National Oil Exchange Corporation (NOEC) shall be established. The NOEC shall determine the country's total monthly requirements for refined petroleum products, and shall exclusively handle all the purchases, storages and distributions thereof to distributors, wholesalers, retailers and big bulk consumers throughout the country.
rows.status: Substituted by HB12052

rows.author: A010
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING DUAL CITIZENSHIP TO AMERICANS AND OTHER FOREIGN CITIZENS WHO ARE FORMER FILIPINOS OR OF FILIPINO ANCESTRY UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The rationale behind this measure is to allow the Filipino expatriates to reacquire  or acquire, as the case maybe, their Filipino citizenship in order that the millions  of these expatriates abroad can be encouraged or enticed to invest in the Philippines, and in the process, shore up the country's economy with the infusion of new capital into its economic mainstream.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1999-11-15

rows.author: C028
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION, SUPERVISION AND PROFESSIONALIZA TION OF THE PRACTICE, LICENSING AND REGISTRATION OF SANITARIANS
rows.abstract: "The Sanitarians Professionaliza tion Act". The Act has the following objectives: (a) the promotion, development and professionaliza tion of sanitary inspection; and (b) the supervision and licensing of sanitary inspectors/sani tarians.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 1999-11-15

rows.author: A100
rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTORING THE TAX EXEMPTION PRIVILEGES OF LOCAL WATER DISTRICTS UNDER SECTION 46 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 198, AS AMENDED AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Section 46 of P.D. 198, as amended, granting tax exemption privileges to local waster districts is hereby restored and shall be effective for a period of ten (10) years from approval of this Act. Water districts shall likewise be exmepted from the provision of R.A. 7656 requiring government-owne d and-controlled corporations (GOCCs) to remit 50% of their annual net oincome to the National Government, Provided, that the amount supposed to be remitted, is utilized  by the water district concerned, for the continuing expansion and improvement of its system.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 1999-11-15

rows.author: A049
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN THE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY POPULARIZATION PROGRAM THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE PHILIPPINE SCIENCE CENTRUM AS THE NATIONAL SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY LEARNING CENTER/MUSEUM AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Philippine Science Centrum Act of 1999". Rationale: Today, science and technology are becoming entrenched in institutions, intellectual life and public policy. Science and Technology have become a fact of life. However, the situation may difer between industrialized and developing countries. That is why we have to redouble our effort to catch up with the rest of the world in terms of technological advancement and preparation, because these are our "bridges to development."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 1999-11-15

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A UNIFORM SYSTEM OF RETIREMENT AND SEPARATION BENEFIT FOR THE UNIFORMED PERSONNEL OF THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT, AMENDING SECTION 34 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8551, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "DILG Uniformed Ppersonnel Retirement and Separation Benefit System of 1999".  The proposed bill is a consolidation of various existing laws pertaining to the retirement and separation benefits previously received, extended, ganted and entitled to receive by former members of the defunct PC and INP before the creation of PNP, BFP and BJMP. There is a perceived need to clarify, restore and to provide some of the uniformed personnel of the DILG, since the merger of the defunct PC and INP under RA6975 has brought to for some problems pertaining to retirement which is imperative to be addressed through an appropriate legislation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 1999-11-15

rows.abstract: The proposed Council shall (1) establish national policies, rules and regulations in the implementation of the Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW) Convention of 1978, As Amended; (2) set guidelines and coordinate activitiesof the member-agencies in the implementation thereof.

rows.abstract: NO BRAND NAME SHALL BE ADDED TO THE PRESCRIPTION. rows.abstract: One of the anticipated results of the implementation of the Comprehensive Land Reform Program (CARP) is the generation of maximized productivity from ther land areas parceled out to the beneficiaries through better crop selection and rotation, the application of quality seeds, and the employment of modern farming methods. Apparently, after more than twn (10) years since the implementation of the CARP, the agricultural productivity improvement effect of the land reform program leaves much to bedesired. >This bill seeks to accelerate agricultural productivity and food production by allowing corporations to utilize lands belonging to Agricultural REform beneficiaries concerned and the Department of Agrarian REform as parties and signatoriesto the contract.

rows.abstract: "Soilless Agricultural Act of 1999". More than just an innovative vehicle for increased food production, soilless farming or hydroponics holds the promise of increased production, employment and income not only for traditional rural farmers but alsofor the unemployed and under-employed urban dwellers as well-provided, that our farming scientists and researchers are able to adapt soilless farming to local conditions using locally available equipment and materials; and provided, further, that reserachers on soilless farming and its local adaptation are adequately disseminated nationwide, especially to the urban populations, for information, guidance and effective implementation.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING MONOPOLIES, ATTEMPT TO MONOPOLIZE AN INDUSTRY OR LINE OF COMMERCE, MANIPULATION OF PRICES OF COMMODITIES, ASSET ACQUISITION AND INTERLOCKING MEMBERSHIPS IN THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF COMPETING CORPORATE BODIES AND PRICE DISCRIMINATION AMONG CUSTOMERS, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES (anti-trust)
rows.abstract: "Philippine Anti-Trust Act of 1999". Rationale: Through time, the Philippine economy has retained oligopolistic and monopolistic features. Some of these features have remained persistent even today, existent in certain sectors of the economy, the government's liberalization program notwithstanding .> Unfortunately, the persistence of oligopoly and monopoly economically disenfranchise our citizens, both consuderms and producers. Genrally, this economic structure contributes to the shrinkage of the people's purchasing power, due mainly to uncompetitively prices goods and services. > This bill therefore seeks to address this problem by penalizing combinations or conspiracies in restraint of trade and all forms of artificial manipulations thatt inhibit free market competition.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 1999-11-22

rows.abstract: Rationale: With the growing global awareness on the dangers of pollution poased by the worldwide maritime carriage of oil bulk, the "1992 Civil Liability Convention" (CLC) and the "1992 Fund Convention" (Fund) were adopted in London on November 27,1992.
